For more than an hour the little old gentleman remained absorbed in his reflections; then he seized pen and paper and made various notes. He was evidently drafting a rather complicated plan. He now and again ran his pen through what he had written and substituted other words.

arxiv-2012-03155.title: Saturation Numbers for Minors
arxiv-2012-03155.creator: Max Aires
arxiv-2012-03155.description: Abstract The saturation number sat ​ ( n , ℱ ) \text{sat}(n,\mathcal{F}) is the minimum number of edges in any graph which does not contain a member of ℱ \mathcal{F} as a subgraph, but will if any edge is added. We give a few upper and lower bounds for saturation numbers for minors.

arxiv-2108-11358.title: Fast multi-qubit gates through simultaneous two-qubit gates
arxiv-2108-11358.creator: Xiu Gu, Jorge Fernández-Pendás, Pontus Vikstål, Tahereh Abad, Christopher Warren, Andreas Bengtsson, Giovanna Tancredi, Vitaly Shumeiko, Jonas Bylander, Göran Johansson, Anton Frisk Kockum
arxiv-2108-11358.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiu Gu, Jorge Fernández-Pendás, Pontus Vikstål, Tahereh Abad, Christopher Warren, Andreas Bengtsson, Giovanna Tancredi, Vitaly Shumeiko, Jonas Bylander, Göran Johansson, Anton Frisk Kockum. Near-term quantum computers are limited by the decoherence of qubits to only being able to run low-depth quantum circuits with acceptable fidelity. This severely restricts what quantum algorithms can be compiled and implemented on such devices.

arxiv-2110-06003.title: Impact of delay classes on the data structure in IOTA
arxiv-2110-06003.creator: Andreas Penzkofer, Olivia Saa and Daria Dziubałtowska
arxiv-2110-06003.description: Abstract In distributed ledger technologies (DLTs) with a directed acyclic graph (DAG) data structure, a message-issuing node can decide where to append that message and, consequently, how to grow the DAG. This DAG data structure can typically be decomposed into two pools of messages: referenced messages and unreferenced messages (tips).

arxiv-2209-01779.title: Representation Learning for Non-Melanoma Skin Cancer using a Latent Autoencoder
arxiv-2209-01779.creator: Simon M. Thomas
arxiv-2209-01779.description: Abstract Generative learning is a powerful tool for representation learning, and shows particular promise for problems in biomedical imaging. However, in this context, sampling from the distribution is secondary to finding representations of real images, which often come with labels and explicitly represent the content and quality of the target distribution.

arxiv-2210-00169.title: Multi-stage Progressive Compression of Conformer Transducer for On-device Speech Recognition
arxiv-2210-00169.creator: Jash Rathod, Nauman Dawalatabad, Shatrughan Singh, Dhananjaya Gowda
arxiv-2210-00169.description: Abstract The smaller memory bandwidth in smart devices prompts development of smaller Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models. To obtain a smaller model, one can employ the model compression techniques. Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular model compression approach that has shown to achieve smaller model size with relatively lesser degradation in the model performance.

arxiv-2402-14831.title: Roles of Energy and Entropy in Multiscale Dynamics and Thermodynamics
arxiv-2402-14831.creator: Miroslav Grmela
arxiv-2402-14831.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Miroslav Grmela. Multiscale thermodynamics is a theory of relations among levels of description. Energy and entropy are its two main ingredients. Their roles in the time evolution describing approach of a level (starting level) to another level involving less details (target level) is examined on several examples, including the level on which macroscopic systems are seen as composed of microscopic particles, mesoscopic levels as kinetic theory of ideal and van der Waals gases, fluid mechanics, the level of chemical kinetics, and the level of

arxiv-2404-04890.title: A Unified Diffusion Framework for Scene-aware Human Motion Estimation from Sparse Signals
arxiv-2404-04890.creator: Jiangnan Tang 1 Jingya Wang 1,2, Kaiyang Ji 1 Lan Xu 1,2 Jingyi Yu 1,2 Ye Shi 1,2, 1 ShanghaiTech University 2 Shanghai Engineering Research Center of Intelligent Vision and Imaging {tangjn2022, wangjingya, jiky, xulan1, yujingyi, shiye}@shanghaitech.edu.cn
arxiv-2404-04890.description: Abstract Estimating full-body human motion via sparse tracking signals from head-mounted displays and hand controllers in 3D scenes is crucial to applications in AR/VR. One of the biggest challenges to this task is the one-to-many mapping from sparse observations to dense full-body motions, which endowed inherent ambiguities.

arxiv-2404-17120.title: Talking Nonsense: Probing Large Language Models’ Understanding of Adversarial Gibberish Inputs
arxiv-2404-17120.creator: Valeriia Cherepanova, James Zou
arxiv-2404-17120.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) exhibit excellent ability to understand human languages, but do they also understand their own language that appears gibberish to us? In this work we delve into this question, aiming to uncover the mechanisms underlying such behavior in LLMs.

arxiv-2502-09317.title: Analog charged black hole formation via percolation: Exploring cosmic censorship and Hoop conjecture
arxiv-2502-09317.creator: Nitesh Jaiswal, S. Shankaranarayanan
arxiv-2502-09317.description: Abstract We investigate an analog model of charged black hole (BH) formation using the framework of classical percolation. By analyzing the scaling behavior of key quantities, including surface gravity and Komar mass, we establish a robust correspondence between this analog system and gravitational collapse in general relativity.

arxiv-2502-12296.title: Temporal Coarse Graining for Classical Stochastic Noise in Quantum Systems
arxiv-2502-12296.creator: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, N. Tobias Jacobson
arxiv-2502-12296.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tameem Albash, Steve Young, N. Tobias Jacobson. Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for 1 / f 1/f noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise.

arxiv-2504-12791.title: Probing the topological protection of edge states in multilayer tungsten ditelluride with the superconducting proximity effect
arxiv-2504-12791.creator: X. Ballu 1,5 , Z. Dou 1,4 , L. Bugaud 1 , R. Delagrange 1 , A. Bernard 1 , Ratnadwip Singha 2,3 , L. M. Schoop 2 , R. J. Cava 2 , R. Deblock 1 , Sophie Guéron 1 , H. Bouchiat 1 and M. Ferrier 1
arxiv-2504-12791.description: Abstract The topology of WTe 2 , a transition metal dichalcogenide with large spin-orbit interactions, is thought to combine type II Weyl semimetal and second-order topological insulator (SOTI) character. The SOTI character should endow WTe 2 multilayer crystals with topologically protected helical states at its hinges, and, indeed, 1D states have been detected thanks to Josephson interferometry.

arxiv-2507-03277.title: Magnetic, charge and orbital properties of pure and Sr-doped La 2 NiO 4 and its pressure evolutions
arxiv-2507-03277.creator: Han-Yu Wang, Shu-Hong Tang, Xiao-Teng Huang, Ya-Min Quan, Xian-Long Wang, Yan-Ling Li, Da-Yong Liu, H.-Q. Lin, Zhi Zeng, Liang-Jian Zou
arxiv-2507-03277.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Han-Yu Wang, Shu-Hong Tang, Xiao-Teng Huang, Ya-Min Quan, Xian-Long Wang, Yan-Ling Li, Da-Yong Liu, H.-Q. Lin, Zhi Zeng, Liang-Jian Zou. Recent discovery of unconventional superconductivity on multilayer nickelates under high pressure have stimulated great interest. The magnetic and charge configurations in the normal phase of multilayer nickelates which closely relate to the spin-charge fluctuations remain under strongly debated.

arxiv-2509-01170.title: ADMP-GNN: Adaptive Depth Message Passing GNN DOI: 10.1145/3746252.3761009 Conference: Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; November 10–14, 2025; Seoul, Republic of Korea Proceedings of the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and K
arxiv-2509-01170.creator: Yassine Abbahaddou, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros, Johannes F. Lutzeyer, Michalis Vazirgiannis
arxiv-2509-01170.description: Abstract . Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be highly effective in various graph learning tasks. A key characteristic of GNNs is their use of a fixed number of message-passing steps for all nodes in the graph, regardless of each node’s diverse computational needs and characteristics.

arxiv-2601-12670.title: Investigation of deuteron-like singly bottomed dibaryon resonances
arxiv-2601-12670.creator: Yuxuan Du 1, Yanyue Pan 1, Xinmei Zhu 2, Zhiyun Tan 3, Hongxia Huang 1, Jialun Ping 1
arxiv-2601-12670.description: Abstract We perform a systematical investigation of the existence of the deuteron-like singly bottomed dibaryon resonance states with strangeness S = − 1 , − 3 , − 5 S=-1,~-3,~-5 in the chiral quark model. Two resonance states with strangeness S = − 1 S=-1 are obtained in the baryon-baryon scattering process.

arxiv-2602-07370.title: Privately Learning Decision Lists and a Differentially Private Winnow
arxiv-2602-07370.creator: Mark Bun, William Fang
arxiv-2602-07370.description: Abstract We give new differentially private algorithms for the classic problems of learning decision lists and large-margin halfspaces in the PAC and online models. In the PAC model, we give a computationally efficient algorithm for learning decision lists with minimal sample overhead over the best non-private algorithms.

arxiv-2606-00757.creator: Danial Saber, Amirali Salehi-Abari

plos-pone-0004762.creator: Daniel Y. Little, Lu Chen
plos-pone-0004762.description: PLOS ONE research article. The structure and function of a protein is dependent on coordinated interactions between its residues. The selective pressures associated with a mutation at one site should therefore depend on the amino acid identity of interacting sites. Mutual information has previously been ap

pmc-10599020.title: Zone 2/3 lesion and emergency repair as potential mortality predictors of TEVAR for thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysm
pmc-10599020.creator: Hui Wang, Chang Shu, Tun Wang, Hao He, Xin Li, Quanming Li, Yuan Peng, Lunchang Wang, Likun Sun
pmc-10599020.description: ObjectiveThoracic aortic pseudoaneurysm (TAP) is an uncommon but life-threatening condition. The present study aimed to investigate the early and midterm clinical outcome of TAP patients following TEVAR and identify potential mortality predictors.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed a series of 37 eligible patients with TAP admitted to our hospital from July 2010 to July 2020. We explored their baseline, perioperative and follow-up data.

pmc-10649327.title: Reinforcement-Learning-Based Localization of Hippocampus for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection
pmc-10649327.creator: Aditya Raj, Golrokh Mirzaei, Zhuhuang Zhou
pmc-10649327.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder primarily impacting memory and cognitive functions. The hippocampus serves as a key biomarker associated with AD. In this study, we present an end-to-end automated approach for AD detection by introducing a reinforcement-learning-based technique to localize the hippocampus within structural MRI images.

pmc-11341174.title: P16 Analysis of antibiotic resistance in wounded servicemen with infectious complications
pmc-11341174.creator: Oksana Viltsaniuk, Viktor Syvak, Nataliia Tkachuk
pmc-11341174.description: BackgroundThe problem of antibiotic resistance has now become a global challenge. Infectious complications are the cause of death in 80% of wounded soldiers whose deaths occur late after a military injury. This confirms that the fight against wound infection is one of the priority tasks in the treatment of combat trauma.

pmc-11355395.title: Adolescents Hospitalized in an Acute Psychiatric Ward: The Difference between Males and Females in the Pre- and Pandemic/Post-Pandemic Periods
pmc-11355395.creator: Rosaria Di Lorenzo, Pietro Bonasegla, Alice Bardelli Canzio, Martina Morgante, Sergio Rovesti, Paola Ferri
pmc-11355395.description: (1) Background: The pandemic lowered by 10% the psychological wellness among adolescents worldwide. (2) Methods: This observational retrospective study compared the demographic and clinical variables of male and female adolescents hospitalized in an acute psychiatric ward during the pre-pandemic, from 1 July 2017 to 28 February 2020, and the pandemic/post-pandemic, from 1 March 2020 to 30 June 2023.

pmc-11446682.title: Survey on the knowledge and practices in anorexia of aging diagnosis and management in Japan
pmc-11446682.creator: Sahoko Takagi, Shosuke Satake, Ken Sugimoto, Masafumi Kuzuya, Masahiro Akishita, Hidenori Arai, Ivan Aprahamian, Andrew J Coats, Tatiana Klompenhouwer, Stefan D Anker, Hidetaka Wakabayashi
pmc-11446682.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAnorexia of aging (AA) is a condition in older adults that includes loss of appetite and reduced food intake. There is a lack of detailed analysis of the potential influence of educational initiatives in addressing AA.

pmc-11591429.title: Conflict and Intimacy in Emerging Adults’ Romantic Relationships and Depressive Symptoms: The Mediating Role of Identity and Couple Satisfaction
pmc-11591429.creator: Federica Graziano, Sofia Mastrokoukou, Elena Cattelino, Luca Rollè, Emanuela Calandri, Emanuela Confalonieri, Gaia Cuccì
pmc-11591429.description: Romantic relationships in emerging adulthood may be associated with depression, but the role of possible mediators of this relationship remains to be explored. The present study tested a serial mediation model where intimacy and conflict in romantic relationships were predictors of depressive symptoms through the mediation of couple satisfaction and identity satisfaction.

pmc-11643755.title: Additive Manufacturing of Binary and Ternary Oxide Systems Using Two-Photon Polymerization and Low-Temperature Sintering
pmc-11643755.creator: Halima El Aadad, Hicham El Hamzaoui, Yves Quiquempois, Marc Douay
pmc-11643755.description: Multicomponent oxide systems have many applications in different fields such as optics and medicine. In this work, we developed new hybrid photoresists based on a combination of an organic acrylate resin and an inorganic sol, suitable for 3D printing via two-photon polymerization (2PP). The inorganic sol contained precursors of a binary SiO2-CaO or a ternary SiO2-CaO-P2O5 system.

pmc-12429130.title: Isometric Conditioning Activity and Jump Performance: Impact of Training Status in Male Participants
pmc-12429130.creator: Jakub Jarosz, Andrzej Szwarc
pmc-12429130.description: Background/Objectives: Post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) is an acute neuromuscular phenomenon influenced by training status, yet evidence regarding its response to isometric conditioning activity (ICA) across different athletic populations remains inconclusive. This study investigated the acute effects of ICA on countermovement jump (CMJ) performance in trained (T) versus highly trained (HT) male participants.

pmc-12553064.title: Unmet supportive care needs among head and neck cancer survivors beyond 5 years after diagnosis: a multinational cohort study
pmc-12553064.creator: Femke Jansen, Simone EJ Eerenstein, Katherine J Taylor, Cecilie D Amdal, Kristin Bjordal, Guro L Astrup, Bente B Herlofson, Fréderic Duprez, Ricardo R Gama, Alexandre A Jacinto, Eva Hammerlid, Melissa Scricciolo, Giuseppe Fanetti, Orlando Guntinas-Lichius, Johanna Inhestern, Tatiana Dragan, Alexande
pmc-12553064.description: SummaryBackgroundThis study investigates unmet supportive care needs (SCNs) among head and neck cancer (HNC) survivors beyond 5 years after diagnosis and examines the association with sociodemographic, clinical and lifestyle factors, and differences in European and non-European regions and healthcare systems.

pmc-12795785.title: Evaluating Research Preparedness and Skill Gaps Among Osteopathic Medical Students Pursuing Surgical Specialties
pmc-12795785.creator: Skylarr A Beerman, Brenton Stucki, Ryan Wong, Vincent S Alexander, Andrew Vogel, Matthew A Heard, Tyler J Wallen
pmc-12795785.description: ObjectivesThe objective of this study is to evaluate osteopathic medical students’ self-reported research experiences, skill levels, and professional goals. This study specifically aimed to assess how students perceive their readiness to engage in research, explore the barriers they face in translating motivation into scholarly productivity, and identify which research tasks students feel most and least confident performing.

pmc-12817863.title: Rehospitalization risk in community-dwelling schizophrenia patients receiving paliperidone palmitate: a retrospective cohort study in urban China
pmc-12817863.creator: Cheng-Feng Liu, Jiao-Lian Yuan, Juan Cheng, Jing-Lu Lu, Wei-Yun Wang, Shao-Ling Zhong, Chu-Hong Lu, Li Qing, Ying Xu, Liang Zhou, Yan-Fang Guo
pmc-12817863.description: BackgroundWhile long-acting injectable paliperidone palmitate (PP-LAI) improves treatment adherence in schizophrenia, rehospitalization risks persist under community management. This study identified factors influencing rehospitalization in community-dwelling schizophrenia patients receiving PP-LAI.MethodsA retrospective cohort study included 560 patients from 124 communities in Shenzhen (16 September 2022–15 September 2024). Data were extracted from medical databases. The primary outcome was rehospitalization due to psychiatric relapse.

pmc-13007373.title: Prompt injection in manuscripts: exploiting loopholes or crossing ethical lines?
pmc-13007373.creator: Shuchen Tang, Zilong Li
pmc-13007373.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe integration of AI in academic publishing has raised significant ethical concerns, particularly regarding the practice of prompt injection, where hidden instructions are embedded in manuscripts to manipulate AI responses in the peer review process.MethodsThis study employed a mixed-methods approach, combining a comprehensive content analysis of academic integrity guidelines with a survey of 194 stakeholders, including authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors from various academic fields.

pmc-13188472.title: Guideline-concordant care and outcomes for pediatric malaria cases: descriptive evidence from pharmacy-based fever management in Kenya
pmc-13188472.creator: Maria Dieci, Carolyne Nekesa, Nettah Isavwa Kayaro, Jessica Vernon, Ilana Graetz, Kate Winskell, Janet R. Cummings
pmc-13188472.description: BackgroundFebrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. In Kenya, pharmacies are a common first point of care for childhood fevers, yet important questions remain about the quality of care provided in these settings and how consistently it aligns with national malaria treatment guidelines.

pmc-13320050.title: Missed achilles tendon injury in superficial laceration: A diagnostic pitfall
pmc-13320050.creator: Jeffrey Byrd, Sreenivasulu Metikala, Madana Vallem, Khalid Hasan
pmc-13320050.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A thorough exploration of traumatic wound is critical to accurately assess the severity of the injury. The authors report a case of a missed achilles tendon injury diagnosed as a superficial laceration in the emergency department.

pmc-13441443.title: Does CD30 loss preclude the diagnosis of anaplastic lymphoma kinase-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma? Insights from a rare case
pmc-13441443.creator: Wenjie Wang, Xiaolong Sui, Guohua Yu
pmc-13441443.description: CD30 positivity serves as a critical diagnostic hallmark for anaplastic lymphoma kinase positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK+ ALCL); however, rare cases with partial or complete loss of CD30 expression present diagnostic challenges. We report a unique case with two morphologically and immunophenotypically distinct subpopulations within the same tumor: A typical CD30-positive component and a CD30-negative counterpart.
